claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA replaces raw attention-mass ranking with a closed-form score that measures how much each sparse unit reduces matrix-product approximation error.
claims.claim_summary: MASA ranks sparse units by closed-form reduction in matrix-product approximation error

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As a theory-grounded plug-in correction, MASA can be added to existing sparse attention frameworks without changing their sparse kernels or budgets.
claims.claim_summary: MASA plugs into existing sparse attention frameworks without changing kernels or budgets

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Extensive experiments across multiple sparse attention methods, benchmarks, and LLM backbones show consistent accuracy gains, supporting both MASA and the matrix-approximation view of sparse attention.
claims.claim_summary: MASA yields consistent accuracy gains across methods, benchmarks, and LLM backbones

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Based on this view, we propose Matrix Approximation Sparse Attention (MASA), a theory-grounded plug-in correction for sparse attention.
claims.claim_summary: The authors propose MASA as a plug-in correction for sparse attention

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA keeps the sparse units, kernels, and budgets of existing sparse attention methods, but replaces their raw attention-mass ranking with a closed-form score derived from matrix-product approximation error.
claims.claim_summary: MASA preserves baseline kernels and budgets while swapping mass ranking for matrix-error scoring

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As a result, MASA can be added to diverse sparse attention frameworks without changing their implementation interface.
claims.claim_summary: MASA integrates into diverse sparse attention frameworks without modifying implementation interfaces

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We identify a long-standing selection mismatch in sparse attention: existing magnitude-based rules approximate the attention matrix entrywise, while the Transformer uses attention through matrix multiplication.
claims.claim_summary: Identifies that prior sparse attention rules approximate matrices entrywise rather than through multiplication

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We propose MASA, a theory-grounded plug-in scoring method that ranks sparse units by their closed-form reduction in matrix-product approximation error.
claims.claim_summary: Proposes MASA to rank sparse units by closed-form matrix-product error reduction

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA can be integrated into existing sparse attention baselines while keeping their sparse kernels and budgets unchanged.
claims.claim_summary: MASA integrates into existing baselines without changing sparse kernels or budgets

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Under matched settings with the original baselines, MASA gives consistent accuracy gains, supporting both the proposed method and the matrix-approximation view of sparse attention.
claims.claim_summary: MASA achieves consistent accuracy gains under matched baseline settings

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA therefore does not require a new full-resolution dense attention map beyond the information used for sparse-unit ranking.
claims.claim_summary: MASA operates without requiring a new full-resolution dense attention map

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This computation only uses matrix products and score matrices at the profile resolution, without materializing the N × N × r contribution tensor.
claims.claim_summary: MASA computes scores at profile resolution without materializing the large contribution tensor

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA improves all eight matched average scores across three sparse methods, three benchmark suites, and both Llama- and Qwen-family backbones.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves all eight matched average scores across methods, benchmarks, and backbones

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On InfiniteBench, MASA raises FlexPrefill-Llama from 47.14 to 47.99 against a full-attention score of 48.06, recovering approximately 92% of the original average-score deficit.
claims.claim_summary: MASA raises FlexPrefill-Llama on InfiniteBench to 47.99, recovering 92% of deficit

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On RULER, MASA raises SeerAttention from 87.60 to 88.09, moving it from below the dense reference to above it.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves SeerAttention on RULER from 87.60 to 88.09, surpassing full attention

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For FlexPrefill-Llama on RULER, replacing the ranking score adds 0.76 points, exceeding the original method's 0.48-point advantage over full attention and increasing that advantage to 1.24 points.
claims.claim_summary: MASA adds 0.76 points to FlexPrefill-Llama on RULER, increasing its advantage to 1.24

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across the four RULER configurations at 32K, 64K, and 128K, MASA improves 11 of 12 matched length-level scores.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves 11 of 12 matched length-level scores on RULER across 32K–128K contexts

claims.claim_text_verbatim: At 128K, MASA improves MInference, SeerAttention, FlexPrefill-Llama, and FlexPrefill-Qwen by 1.28, 0.48, 1.45, and 2.16 points, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: At 128K on RULER, MASA improves four configurations by up to 2.16 points

claims.claim_text_verbatim: At 64K, the gains reach 2.16 points for FlexPrefill-Llama and 3.65 points for FlexPrefill-Qwen.
claims.claim_summary: At 64K context on RULER, MASA improves FlexPrefill on Qwen by 3.65 points

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On LongBench, MASA improves SeerAttention's 8K+ score from 52.69 to 53.16.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves SeerAttention's 8K+ score on LongBench from 52.69 to 53.16

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The evaluated MASA configurations reduce normalized squared output error in all four framework–backbone pairs, providing direct empirical support for matrix-product preservation.
claims.claim_summary: MASA reduces normalized squared attention output error across all four evaluated configurations

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across MInference, SeerAttention, FlexPrefill-Llama, and FlexPrefill-Qwen, replacing the original ranking score with MASA adds empirically negligible overhead relative to the sparse attention runtime and remains far below the dense attention cost.
claims.claim_summary: Replacing ranking with MASA adds negligible latency overhead across all evaluated frameworks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: First, raw MASA already improves the original sparse baseline in several settings, which supports the matrix-product scoring objective itself.
claims.claim_summary: Raw MASA improves baseline performance in several settings without norm control

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The relative reductions are 0.41% for MInference, 2.10% for SeerAttention, and 2.34% and 7.17% for FlexPrefill on Llama and Qwen, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: MASA reduces output approximation error by up to 7.17% across baselines

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across multiple sparse baselines, benchmarks, and LLM backbones, MASA gives consistent gains under matched settings with negligible latency overhead.
claims.claim_summary: MASA consistently improves accuracy across baselines and benchmarks with negligible overhead
